main_results: All three targeted runs completed on mclab-3090 with fixed read_topk=4 and the new read-side telemetry present in validation logs.
cb256-r8 readk4 seed123 final/best hard is 0.992, filling the strongest historical local-positive gap for the cb256-r8 readk4 formalization set.
cb256-r4 readk4 seed123 final/best hard is 0.965, filling the cb256-r4 readk4 seed123 formalization gap.
cb128-r8 readk4 s125 repeat final/best hard is 0.967, so this repeat did not reproduce the earlier 0.609 collapse; it weakens but does not erase the cb128-r8 rerun-risk claim.
best-final gap is 0.0 for all three runs; this wave is not a late-drift failure case.
cb128-r8 reaches high hard accuracy but has final m_norm_max 13.8, above the prior m_norm>12 no-official redline, so it remains a boundary/risk case rather than a clean positive.
caveats: This wave has no same-wave readk2 control; compare against historical readk2/readk4 rows only as contextual evidence.
Only seed123 was added for cb256-r4 and cb256-r8; full three-seed cb256 formalization requires combining with historical readk4 rows.
Candidate churn is still not implemented; read-side telemetry now covers margin, entropy and selected mass but not churn.
Raw logs and generated configs have been mirrored to mclab-2080ti under ignored paths and sha256 verified; swanlog backups and checkpoints remain on mclab-3090 under ignored paths.
This is exploratory/formalization support and is not written to the canonical gd-residual-v1 official ledger.
